result:
Post revisions now work: each successful edit keeps the version it replaced, authors can view and restore them, and deleting a post removes its history. `bun run typecheck` passes, and `bun test` passes with 8 tests, 6 of them new. I didn't boot the app, so the new page has only been checked by the tests, not viewed in a browser.

- **Storage:** a new `post_revisions` table (`id`, `post_id`, `title`, `excerpt`, `body`, `created_at` as ISO text) is defined in `db/schema.ts`, with a migration generated in `db/migrations/20260929141624_add_post_revisions/`. There's also a new `PostRevision` model and a `PostRevisionResource`.
- **Keeping versions:** in `PostController.update`, the post's current title, excerpt and body are saved as a revision in the same transaction as the update, so both happen or neither does. Nothing is kept on create, or when an edit is refused for bad input or permission.
- **Restore:** it goes through the same save path as an edit, so the version being replaced also becomes a revision and the restored one stays in the list.
- **New routes:** `GET /posts/:id/revisions` renders the new `posts/Revisions` page, with `revisions: [{ id, title, createdAt, … }]` newest first. `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` restores and redirects to `/posts/:id`.
- **Access:** both routes sit behind login (guests go to `/login`) and use the same author-only check as editing, so other users get 403. The revision lookup is limited to the post in the URL, so a revision from another post gets 404, even when the same author owns both.
- **Delete:** `destroy` deletes the post's revisions explicitly in the same transaction as the post. The table also has `ON DELETE CASCADE`, but SQLite only applies that when foreign keys are turned on, so I didn't rely on it.
- **Page and link:** the post page now shows the author a "Revisions" link next to Edit. The generated `.guren/*.gen.ts` files were regenerated with `bun run codegen` and are part of the change.

The new tests in `tests/PostRevisions.test.ts` run against the test database and cover the worked example (First → Second → Third, then restoring First), refused edits, the 403, `/login` and 404 cases, and delete.
